newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's coalition partners agree on power swap.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's coalition partners agree on power swap.

text.p: Turkey's government coalition partners have agreed to hand over the premiership from Islamist prime minister, Necmettin Erbakan, to conservative Tansu Ciller, a senior MP from Ciller's party said late on Thursday.
Ciller will become prime minister on June 18 and an announcement would be made on June 17, Hasan Ekinci, deputy chairman of Ciller's True Path Party, said on the private ATV channel.
But it was unclear how the handover would be brought about since it would need to be approved by the president and parliament, where the 11-month-old coalition now lacks a majority.
Erbakan's government has been hamstrung by disputes over religious activism since the army called in February for a crackdown on Moslem revivalism.

Erbakan, NATO member Turkey's first Islamist leader, earlier said he would transfer power to Ciller by the end of this month under a government plan for snap elections to try to resolve the army dispute.
But the allies disagreed on the timing of the handover.

True Path, a pro-Western party, said it would withdraw from the government if Ciller, now the foreign minister, were not made prime minister by June 18 under a plan to deflect criticism of the alliance by the influential generals.

An MP from Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party deserted the party on Thursday and declared himself an independent, leaving the coalition with 274 MPs in the 550-seat assembly, where two seats are vacant.
